limitations: No ApoMarioHighscore source exists in the inspected tree, so its exact file format, Path selection, synchronization model, and public symbol anchors remain to be created.
The repository evidence does not establish a shared-level server client beyond ApoIO's generic URL-capable reader; remote-content reachability into normal scoring remains unresolved.
The exact human-player selection policy for one-player versus two-player runs is not fully specified by the task; ApoMarioLevel#setAnalysis contains both one-player and two-player scoring branches.
The existing code exposes mutable setters and debug/AI paths that permit local score tampering; no anti-cheat authenticity mechanism was observed.

Player name displayed on the highscore board
Run state to highscore record
nodes.sink: ApoMarioHighscore.storeRun(...) and subsequent persisted highscore output.
nodes.source: ApoMarioPlayer#getPoints(), ApoMarioLevel#getPassedTime(), and ApoMarioPlayer#getTeamName() at run finalization.
nodes.untrusted_input: Mutable in-game score, elapsed-time state, and player name; local tampering can alter these values.

nodes.label: Level/replay file content to run state
nodes.sink: ApoMarioLevel state used by scoring and run completion.

nodes.untrusted_input: Local level/replay files and content from a shared level server.

nodes.label: Highscore store file to menu display
nodes.sink: Highscore getters and the dedicated menu panel's Graphics2D rendering.
nodes.source: ApoMarioHighscore persistence reader and record decoder.
nodes.untrusted_input: The file passed to ApoMarioHighscore(Path) can be locally edited, truncated, duplicated, or made oversized.

nodes.label: The score is mutable on ApoMarioPlayer and final scoring is performed in ApoMarioLevel#setAnalysis(boolean), including finish, remaining-time, difficulty, width, and opponent-related point adjustments.
nodes.task_relevance: Highscore must capture the post-adjustment score at run completion rather than an intermediate HUD value.
nodes.verification: Exercise a win and loss and assert the stored score equals the player score after setAnalysis completes.

nodes.label: ApoMarioLevel exposes elapsed time through getPassedTime(), computed from randomLevel.getTime() minus the current countdown time; levelStartTime and time are initialized during level creation.
nodes.task_relevance: The new recordRunEnd(level) must use the level's elapsed-time state and convert it to bounded mm:ss presentation data.
nodes.verification: Test elapsed-time recording at start, mid-run, timeout, win, and loss; include a non-random/editor level.

nodes.label: Player names are represented by ApoMarioPlayer.teamName, set through AI/name handling and rendered directly as text in the game statistics; setNames() refreshes names before a normal game starts.
nodes.task_relevance: The highscore name is display-bound local data and must remain a safe, bounded text value.
nodes.verification: Use names containing control characters, long Unicode text, and null; verify storage and rendering remain bounded and non-crashing.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject the run record or clamp to an explicitly documented safe range; do not persist invalid score, name, or survival-time values.
nodes.label: If recordRunEnd accepts mutable score, name, or elapsed time without validation, local tampering or malformed level-derived values can create forged, negative, overflowing, or inconsistent highscore records.
nodes.task_relevance: The feature explicitly records real run performance and therefore makes these values persistent integrity data.
nodes.verification: Unit-test storeRun with negative and extreme integers, null/empty/oversized/control-character names, and assert invalid records are not persisted.

nodes.failure_behavior: On malformed, truncated, oversized, or unreadable store input, ignore the invalid file and load an empty or last-known-valid in-memory board without throwing into the game loop.
nodes.label: If the user-editable highscore store is parsed permissively, malformed fields, negative counts, oversized names, or truncated records can cause invalid display data, allocation exhaustion, or index misalignment.
nodes.task_relevance: The required Path store is a local file and persists across runs, so its read path is an untrusted input boundary.
nodes.verification: Feed the reader empty, truncated, oversized, negative-count, invalid-UTF-8, and structurally inconsistent files and assert bounded execution with a safe fallback.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject the level before installing it when dimensions, counts, time, coordinates, or entity parameters exceed game limits or are inconsistent.
nodes.label: If level files or shared-server content can choose width, height, time, entities, finish position, or difficulty without bounds, they can manipulate the score calculation or cause excessive allocation before highscore recording.
nodes.task_relevance: The highscore uses level-derived elapsed time and scoring inputs, so untrusted level content reaches the new record path indirectly.
nodes.verification: Test boundary and oversized level files, invalid entity counts, negative dimensions/time, and coordinates outside the level; assert rejection before allocation or scoring.

nodes.failure_behavior: If the level, player, name, or elapsed-time source is unavailable or the mode is replay/editor/simulation, skip recording and leave the existing highscore unchanged.
nodes.label: At the run-finalization operation, recordRunEnd(ApoMarioLevel) must read the final player score after scoring adjustments, the selected human player's name, and elapsed survival time for both clearing and losing; replay/editor/simulation runs must not be recorded as normal player runs.
nodes.task_relevance: This directly implements the requested real score, name, and survival-time behavior at every run end.
nodes.verification: Integration-test win, loss, replay, editor, and simulation paths; assert exactly one normal record only for win/loss and that it contains post-finalization values.

nodes.failure_behavior: Return false and make no in-memory or persistent change for invalid input; otherwise insert one aligned record and sort atomically.
nodes.label: At ApoMarioHighscore.storeRun(int,int,String), validate score and survival time as bounded non-negative values, validate playerName as non-null bounded text without control characters or record delimiters, and maintain aligned name/score/time records sorted by score descending.
nodes.task_relevance: The requested board persists names and performance and requires descending point order.
nodes.verification: Property-test insertion with shuffled scores and malformed values; assert all three getters remain equal-length and scores are descending.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject the whole malformed record/file and fall back to an empty or last-known-valid board; never partially allocate from an unbounded count.
nodes.label: At construction and persistence loading, treat the store file as untrusted structured data: enforce a versioned format, maximum byte/record/name limits, exact field counts, numeric ranges, and aligned records before exposing any getter result.
nodes.task_relevance: The highscore board must survive local file tampering without crashing or displaying structurally corrupted records.
nodes.verification: Mutation-test every field and length boundary and assert the parser either produces a valid bounded board or the specified fallback.

nodes.failure_behavior: Return failure or retain the previous store when serialization, flush, close, or replacement fails; do not expose a partially written file as valid.
nodes.label: At persistence, write a complete validated snapshot of aligned records and make replacement atomic where supported; a failed write must not destroy the prior valid store.
nodes.task_relevance: The board is required to persist across runs, and partial writes could lose or reorder player performance history.
nodes.verification: Inject write, flush, close, and rename failures and assert the previous file remains readable and unchanged.

nodes.failure_behavior: If a getter list is unavailable or inconsistent, render a safe empty-state message and do not index or render partial records.
nodes.label: The dedicated menu highscore panel must render validated getter data only, preserve the score-descending order, display each associated player name and survival time as mm:ss, and remain available after initialization and subsequent menu transitions.
nodes.task_relevance: This implements the requested dedicated view and display behavior without allowing malformed persisted text to affect the game UI.
nodes.verification: Render empty, one-record, tied-score, maximum-record, and malformed-store fallback states; assert order, association, mm:ss formatting, and no exception.

nodes.failure_behavior: On invalid or duplicate input, do not call storeRun; continue the existing analysis transition without modifying highscore state.
nodes.label: At ApoMarioLevel#setAnalysis(boolean), call recordRunEnd only after all point adjustments and before transitioning to analysis; have recordRunEnd derive values from the level/player getters, reject null or non-human modes, and guard against duplicate finalization.
nodes.task_relevance: This binds the feature to the authoritative run-end transition and prevents intermediate or duplicate records.
nodes.verification: Instrument the highscore object and assert one call after score updates, zero calls for duplicate setAnalysis invocations, and no calls for replay/editor/simulation.

nodes.failure_behavior: Return false for out-of-range data and retain the previous bounded list unchanged.
nodes.label: At storeRun, apply fixed limits to record count, name length, score, and survival time before allocation or sorting; use a record object or coordinated tuple so getters cannot become misaligned; format survival time only after validation as mm:ss.
nodes.task_relevance: This prevents malformed run data from corrupting ordering or consuming unbounded memory while implementing the requested display format.
nodes.verification: Stress-test maximum-length names, maximum record count, and extreme integer values; assert bounded allocations and stable getter alignment.

nodes.failure_behavior: Stop parsing and use an empty or last-known-valid board when any bound, syntax, range, or alignment check fails.
nodes.label: At ApoMarioHighscore's Path reader, read no more than the configured maximum bytes and records, parse into temporary bounded tuples, validate all fields, sort only after validation, and expose immutable or defensive-copy getter lists.
nodes.task_relevance: This covers decoding and allocation before the data reaches the dedicated menu view.
nodes.verification: Use malformed-file fuzzing and verify no exception escapes initialization, no oversized collection is created, and getters cannot mutate internal state.

nodes.failure_behavior: Return failure and leave the previous valid level active or load a safe empty level; do not partially install attacker-controlled state.
nodes.label: At ApoMarioLevelIO#readLevel(DataInputStream), validate dimensions and counts before creating the levelEntities array or iterating attacker-controlled loops, validate time and coordinates, and reject inconsistent finish/player data before the level becomes active.
nodes.task_relevance: This protects the run-state source that feeds recordRunEnd and limits file/server-driven denial of service and score manipulation.
nodes.verification: Instrument allocation and level installation and assert invalid headers fail before allocation; test valid files remain compatible.

nodes.failure_behavior: On any failure, delete only the temporary file if safe, retain the previous target, and report false or a controlled failure without crashing the game.
nodes.label: At persistAcrossRuns, serialize only the validated bounded snapshot to a temporary file in the store directory, flush and close it, then atomically move/replace the target when available; synchronize concurrent store/persist operations.
nodes.task_relevance: This preserves persistence availability and record integrity across crashes or overlapping calls.
nodes.verification: Run concurrent persist/store calls and crash/failure simulations; reopen the store and assert it is either the old complete snapshot or the new complete snapshot.

nodes.failure_behavior: Skip inconsistent entries and render a fixed fallback label for invalid names/times; continue rendering the menu.
nodes.label: At the highscore panel render method, iterate only over the minimum common validated length of names, scores, and times, use locale-independent mm:ss formatting, and render names as plain bounded Graphics2D text; do not interpret markup or file control sequences.
nodes.task_relevance: This protects the sink where untrusted persisted names and values become visible UI output.
nodes.verification: Snapshot-test rendering with Unicode, control characters, very long names, inconsistent list sizes, and invalid times.

nodes.label: Inspection did not establish whether the target branch already has a shared-level server client or how ApoMarioHighscore's store Path is selected and scoped; ApoIO supports both local and URL reads, while ApoMarioPanel's visible level/replay paths are local-file based.
nodes.task_relevance: The final implementation must resolve the trust boundary and allowed location for the highscore store before wiring persistence.
nodes.verification: Trace the caller/configuration that supplies the highscore Path and any URL/shared-level implementation; document whether remote content can reach normal play scoring.

nodes.label: Inspection did not establish whether getPassedTime() is valid for every supported level mode: it dereferences randomLevel, while editor level loading can install level data through ApoMarioLevelIO.
nodes.task_relevance: recordRunEnd must choose a defined elapsed-time source for random, editor-loaded, replay, and timeout runs.
nodes.verification: Construct each level mode and call the proposed recordRunEnd path at win, loss, and timeout; verify elapsed time is defined and non-throwing.

summary: Highscore data will flow from mutable run state and player name into a new persistent file, then back through parsing into a menu panel. Existing run finalization is ApoMarioLevel#setAnalysis(boolean), which computes final points, sets win state, and opens analysis; existing menu navigation and rendering provide integration points. Local files, shared level content, and tampered in-game state are untrusted under the fixed desktop threat model.
